questions.prompt: Let the general lead his weary soldiers through the mountains before nightfall.
questions.answer: Dux fessōs mīlitēs per montēs ante noctem dūcat.

questions.prompt: Use that gift of fortune wisely, my friend.
questions.answer: Istō fortūnae mūnere sapienter ūtāre, amīce.

questions.prompt: Let them tell the truth, lest they nourish a lasting infamy.
questions.answer: Vērum dīcant, nē diūturnam īnfāmiam alant.

questions.prompt: Let the prophet speak, for the crowd awaits his words.
questions.answer: Prophēta loquātur, nam turba verba eius exspectat.

questions.prompt: Let the sailors trust the winds, although the sky is growing cloudy.
questions.answer: Nautae ventīs fīdant, quamquam caelum nūbilum fit.

questions.prompt: Live temperately, and shun the avarice of the crowd.
questions.answer: Modestē vīvās, et avāritiam vulgī fugiās.

questions.prompt: Let the old woman rest, for her long life has been full of toils.
questions.answer: Anus requiēscat, nam longa eius vīta labōribus plēna fuit.

questions.prompt: Let the citizens, terrified by the thunderbolt, flee into the temples.
questions.answer: Cīvēs fulmine territī in templa fugiant.

questions.prompt: Take part in the assembly, and defend the freedom of your homeland.
questions.answer: Intersīs conciliō, et lībertātem patriae dēfendās.

questions.prompt: Let them fear the gods, and let them not disdain the sacred rites.
questions.answer: Deōs metuant, nēve sacra dēdignentur.

questions.prompt: Let the poet sing of arms and the deeds of brave men.
questions.answer: Poēta arma et fortium virōrum facta canat.

questions.prompt: Let the leaders, once the omens have been heard, govern the state with prudence.
questions.answer: Ducēs, ōminibus audītīs, rem pūblicam prūdenter regant.

questions.prompt: Embrace virtue while you are young, and flee idle pleasures.
questions.answer: Virtūtem amplexēris dum iuvenis es, et ignāvās voluptātēs fugiās.

questions.prompt: Let the merchant not deceive the ignorant with false weights.
questions.answer: Mercātor ignārōs falsīs ponderibus nē fallat.

questions.prompt: Let the wise man bear old age with a calm mind.
questions.answer: Sapiēns senectam aequō animō ferat.

questions.prompt: Let the guards keep watch through the night, lest the enemy attack the camp.
questions.answer: Custōdēs per noctem vigilent, nē hostēs castra oppugnent.

questions.prompt: Enjoy that good which fortune has given, and complain of nothing.
questions.answer: Istō bonō quod fortūna dedit ūtāre, et nihil querāre.

questions.prompt: Let the king reign justly, lest the citizens plot rebellion.
questions.answer: Rēx iūstē rēgnet, nē cīvēs sēditiōnem mōliantur.

questions.prompt: Consider what is right, and do not scorn the counsel of the old.
questions.answer: Cōgitēs quid rēctum sit, nēve senum cōnsilium spernās.

questions.prompt: Let the students not despise the fleeting labors of learning.
questions.answer: Discipulī flūxōs discendī labōrēs nē contemnant.

questions.prompt: This, however, is the sum of my precept: live with an inferior as you would wish a superior to live with you.
questions.answer: Haec tamen praeceptī meī summa est: sīc cum īnferiōre vīvās quemadmodum tēcum superiōrem velīs vīvere.

questions.prompt: Just so he says: "Let them pay court like clients, like morning-callers!".
questions.answer: Ita inquit prōrsus: “Cōlant tamquam clientēs, tamquam salūtātōrēs!”

questions.prompt: Let some dine with you because they are worthy, and some in order that they may become so; for if there is anything servile in them from base association, the company of more honorable men will shake it out of them.
questions.answer: Quīdam cēnent tēcum quia dignī sunt, quīdam ut sint; sī quid enim in illīs ex sordidā conversātiōne servīle est, honestiōrum convictus excutiet.

questions.prompt: Let no man hinder them from going away.
questions.answer: morātus sit nēmō quō minus abeant.

questions.prompt: You must be careful, dear Tiro.
questions.answer: cautus sīs, mī Tirō.

questions.prompt: Enjoy this blessing while you have it with you.
questions.answer: istō bonō ūtāre, dum adsit.

questions.prompt: Well, if they did gloat over my mishaps, still they ought to have been touched by the danger to Rome.
questions.answer: quod sī meīs incommodīs laetābantur, urbis tamen perīculō commovērentur.
